title: Recovery on Payday — Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan Rules
content:
## Rule of recovery

On each payday the amount due on a Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan is the transfers and fees carrying that payday, net of their returns and reversals, plus any shortfall carried to that payday, less any credit left on the plan by a reversal of an already recovered fee. The employer deducts the amount due from the worker's paycheck under the program's deduction file and the amount the employer reports as deducted is booked as a payroll deduction recovery carrying that payday. When net pay cannot cover the whole amount and the tier allows partial payroll deduction, the employer deducts what net pay covers.

## Shortfalls

When the recoveries for the payday (payroll deductions, voluntary payments and card autorecoveries carrying that payday) are less than the amount due, the difference is booked as one shortfall for that payday with the reason the employer reported: net pay insufficient, deduction not taken or employment ended. A payday's shortfall is booked once.

A shortfall is carried to the worker's next payday, recorded as its carryforward payday, while the carry chain (the number of shortfalls in the chain of carried shortfalls ending at the one booked for that payday, one when no earlier shortfall was carried to it) is no more than the tier's carryforward count; a shortfall that would exceed that limit is not carried and is written off under the write-off rules, and a shortfall with reason employment ended is never carried.

## Card autorecovery

When the tier allows card autorecovery, the plan may also be recovered from the worker's card.

- A card autorecovery debit may be attempted only when the plan's card recovery authorization is true.
- A card autorecovery debit may be attempted only while the worker's Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account status is active.
- A card autorecovery debit may not be attempted before the tier's card autorecovery delay in business days has passed after the payday whose amount fell short. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted forward from the day after that payday.

The debit is for the lesser of the open shortfall and the card's available balance, at most the tier's count of card autorecovery debits per shortfall, and is booked as a card autorecovery pointing to the shortfall and carrying its payday; a debit the card cannot cover in full is never retried for the rest. A shortfall is recovered from the card at most once.

*Delay boundary (hypothetical, two-business-day delay, payday on a Monday with no holiday that week):* the count starts on Tuesday, so the payday plus two business days is Wednesday: an attempt on Wednesday satisfies the rule and one on Tuesday does not.

## Voluntary payment and limits

When the tier allows voluntary repayment the worker may pay part or all of the outstanding balance from their own funds at any time, at least the tier's smallest voluntary payment or the whole balance when smaller, booked as a voluntary payment recovery applied to the oldest unpaid payday first. Recoveries never exceed the outstanding balance, and no interest, late fee or collection charge is ever added to an unrecovered amount.
